今日的费城半导体指数调仓，会对市场造成多大的影响？

其中MU MRVL LRCX AMAT 都会有不同程度的卖出现象

而 $SOXX 有大量的杠杆产品
如 $SOXL $SOXS 

SOX 调权 → 部分半导体股出现被动买卖 → 这些股票和 SOXL 底层 ICE Semiconductor Index 高度重合 → 半导体板块价格波动 → SOXL 按 3 倍放大。

假设 SOXL 规模约 250-300 亿美元级别，目标是 3 倍敞口，那么它背后对应的名义敞口可能是 750-900 亿美元。Yahoo / Robinhood 等页面显示 SOXL 规模大约在 250-300 亿美元附近。

所以 SOXL 的最大风险：

调权当天 MU / MRVL / AMD / NVDA / AVGO 等重合股尾盘异动；
半导体指数如果同方向下跌，SOXL 会被动放大；
如果当天本来就高波动，SOXL 的再平衡可能让尾盘更极端。

————————

（调仓时间可能集中在6/18和6/22两天时间

mentions.text:
Oh look who is bearish $SOXX 

I guess… the bottom is in.

Michael Burry said he thinks its worth trying to go "bargain hunting" in Hong Kong’s stock market after it lagged peers during the global AI rally this year

“It is a particularly good time to look to Hong Kong for cheap stocks that should do well as the shine comes off Korea, Japan & the Soxx”

You're surviving one of the sharpest momentum reversals since the early 1970s. 

Lower than 2001. Lower than 2008-09. Lower than March 2020. Lower than the ~-32 spike around 2021.

That's Goldman's read on the S&P 500 momentum factor. Steepest three-week selloff on record.

Now look at the S&P 500 itself: +0.83% on the month. About 1% off its all-time high. Green tape.

So what actually got hit? Semis. Memory, AI, CPU, photonics.

The index didn't fall. The money just moved.

That's not a thesis breaking. Demand didn't change.

ER season is in full swing. Let's watch the next two weeks closely.

mentions.text:
Let’s measure market sentiment on this side of FinX…

SOXX entered a bear market on July 17, down more than 20% from its June peak.

What are you doing going forward?

I guess we can’t all fit together in the same ride $SOXX $SMH $DRAM

Semi ETFs had a $46bn inflow this year, more than double the previous 9 years combined, in under 8 months.

The ones not wearing their seatbelts are being dropped off, while others are stepping off voluntarily.

I wonder how much spaces like X and Substack have altered how people invest, and whether we are mostly piling into the same names, even if some of us earlier than others.

I ran a poll today with 2,000 responses:

17% are actually selling
55% are holding
28% are buying (I’m here)

Either my side of X/Substack isn’t representative of retail, or we really aren’t done unwinding.

Can’t blame you for not wanting to step off the biggest technological revolution of the past 25 years.

Today is max pain day for me since this momentum unwind started back on June 22 in $SMH and $SOXX.

I agree 100% with TCL’s take.

And if you can't explain why you agree or disagree with it, that's worth sitting with. Conviction you can't articulate usually belongs to someone else.

Today I got rid of the excess margin I was carrying, about 30% of the book. Yes, at a loss.

Moving forward, I won't add anything unless I have the cash to do it.

This might unravel until the end of the year, who knows. Calling the bottom is a fool's errand.

I might be tempted to sell and buy the same holdings back lower. That's how you end up right on direction and holding less stock.

But I'm not going anywhere. When life gets tough I don't take a break. When life gets tough I get tougher. It's the only way I know how to move forward.

Living longer gives you a better perspective on what matters. I'm older than most of my followers on FinX, though not old myself. Which means for a lot of you, this is probably the first time living through something like this.

If you're reading this and feel like you can't take it anymore, the best thing you can do is preserve your mental health, not your capital.

Don't borrow your conviction from me. I've been through a lot of hardship and have always come out the other side.

Regardless of the outcome, I'll be fine. Only because I do the work. Only because I lean on others when I most need it. Only because even if my whole portfolio underperforms the indices, I'll keep pushing forward, and specially surviving one day at the time.

What I'll say to you is this: preserve the most valuable asset you have, which is your health, especially your mental health.

Nothing in this market is worth your health.
